passenger-train.definition: A train used to transport people rather than freight.

freight-train.definition: A train used mainly to transport goods rather than passengers.
freight-train.exampleUsage: A freight train moved containers through the station yard.

high-speed-train.definition: A passenger train designed to travel at very high speeds on suitable rail lines.
high-speed-train.exampleUsage: The high-speed train connects the two cities.

subway.definition: An electric railway operating below the surface of the ground (usually in a city).

train-car.definition: One vehicle or carriage forming part of a train.
train-car.exampleUsage: Passengers entered the second train car.

dining-car.definition: A railway carriage that provides meals and drinks to passengers during a journey.

sleeper-car.definition: A passenger train car containing beds or sleeping compartments for overnight travel.
sleeper-car.exampleUsage: The overnight train includes a sleeper car.

caboose.definition: A car on a freight train for use of the train crew.

monorail.definition: An elevated train that moves around a park.

platform.definition: A raised surface used for equipment, sets, or performances.

track.definition: A distinct selection of music from a recording or a compact disc.

ticket-office.definition: An office where visitors purchase tickets that let them enter a show or attraction.

waiting-room.definition: A room where passengers sit while waiting for a train.
waiting-room.exampleUsage: Travelers waited in the station waiting room.

information-desk.definition: A staffed service point helps visitors in public or institutional buildings find their way, ask questions, and obtain general assistance.

newsstand.definition: A small shop or stand that sells newspapers and magazines.

vending-machine.definition: A machine that dispenses products after a customer inserts payment.
vending-machine.exampleUsage: The vending machine was used during the activity.

restroom.definition: A public room containing toilets and washing facilities.

parking-garage.definition: A building or covered structure with multiple vehicle-parking spaces.
parking-garage.exampleUsage: The station parking garage is connected by a walkway.

taxi-stand.definition: A designated place where taxis wait to pick up passengers.
taxi-stand.exampleUsage: Passengers lined up at the taxi stand.

bus-stop.definition: A designated roadside location where buses collect passengers or let them off, often identified by a sign, shelter, or raised platform.

ticket.definition: A printed or electronic pass that allows entry to a ride or park.

round-trip.definition: A journey that carries someone to a destination and back to the place of departure, or the combined distance or fare for both legs.

one-way.definition: Moving one way means following a single direction, with no change of course or return.

schedule.definition: A plan showing when events or activities will happen.

timetable.definition: A schedule listing events and the times at which they will take place.

departure-board.definition: A display showing scheduled departures, destinations, platforms, and times.
departure-board.exampleUsage: The departure board showed a platform change.

arrival-board.definition: A display showing incoming services, arrival times, and related information.
arrival-board.exampleUsage: The arrival board listed the delayed train.

reservation.definition: Something reserved in advance (as a hotel accommodation or a seat on a plane etc.).

seat-number.definition: A number used to identify a specific passenger seat.

first-class.definition: A higher service class on some trains, usually offering different seating or amenities from standard class.
first-class.exampleUsage: The diagram marks the first-class car.

economy-class.definition: A travel section on a ship, train, or plane that costs less than first class.

pass.definition: Of advancing the ball by throwing it.

turnstile.definition: A gate consisting of a post that acts as a pivot for rotating arms.

signal.definition: An electrical or radio message that carries information.

crossing-gate.definition: A movable barrier that blocks road or pedestrian traffic when a train is approaching a railway crossing.
crossing-gate.exampleUsage: The crossing gate lowered before the train arrived.

bridge.definition: A structure built over water or a low place for people to cross.

tunnel.definition: A narrow passage with an opening at both ends.

overhead-wire.definition: An electrical wire suspended above a railway line to supply power to electric trains.
overhead-wire.exampleUsage: The electric train draws power from the overhead wire.

rail.definition: A metal track on which a train runs.

switch.definition: Railroad track having two movable rails and necessary connections.

buffer-stop.definition: A barrier at the end of a railway track designed to prevent trains from moving beyond the track end.
buffer-stop.exampleUsage: The buffer stop stood at the end of the platform track.

clock-tower.definition: A tower designed with a large clock displayed high on an exterior wall.

conductor.definition: The person who leads a musical group.

engineer.definition: A person who designs and checks technical parts of a building project.
engineer.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "engineer" in an educational description.

porter.definition: United States writer of novels and short stories (1890-1980).

commuter.definition: A passenger train that is ridden primarily by passengers who travel regularly from one place to another.

boarding.definition: The act of passengers and crew getting aboard a ship or aircraft.

departing.definition: That is going out or leaving.

arriving.definition: Getting to a place or the end of a trip.

transferring.definition: To transfer somebody to a different position or location of work.

waiting.definition: The act of waiting (remaining inactive in one place while expecting something).

announcing.definition: In scholarly writing, announcing can serve as a discourse marker that draws attention to the act of revealing information.
